title: Set crediting and weekly targets
summary: How the app turns your sets into weekly totals per muscle, which sets count as hard, what the weekly targets and statuses mean, how the weekly curve works, and how Payoff shows where sets stop paying off in one workout. Every number on this page is quoted from the app's data files.

features: Weekly volume panel and body map (targets.json counting, volume_zones; rules.json weekly_status)
Hard-set rule and set tags in the logger (rules.json logger)
Payoff body map, gauges and per-muscle sheet (rules.json rules[id=payoff])
On-plan check in the weekly review (rules.json review)
app_link.explains: Exactly how a set becomes a number on the board, when a muscle needs sets, and where extra sets in one workout stop paying off.

sections.heading: How sets are counted
body: Every hard set counts toward each muscle the exercise works. The main mover gets a full set; a helper muscle gets part of a set, a bit less when it works further from failure.
Weekly volume is counted at face value: the same sets count the same whether you do them in one workout or spread them over two.

points.text: Ratings below 0.25 are ignored.
Weekly totals are shown rounded to the nearest 0.5; colours and flags use the exact total.
Example: 4 sets of incline dumbbell press plus 3 sets of cable fly give 7 chest sets, because chest is the main mover in both.
In a large meta-regression, counting indirect sets as half a set fit the growth data best. The app's per-exercise ratings are a finer-grained version of that idea.

sections.heading: Which sets count
body: Planned sets on the board are assumed to be hard sets. Logged sets count as hard only when they are close enough to failure.
Set tags change how much a logged set counts. Warm-ups are their own set kind and never count.

points.text: A logged set is hard when it is a working set with at least one rep and RIR 3 or less, or no RIR entered.
You can move that cut-off anywhere from 0 to 5 in settings.
Credit applies only when the set is hard. A tagged set with no RIR uses the tag's default RIR.
Failure: default RIR of 0, and it counts 1.0 hard set. There is no bonus for failure.
Myo-rep match: credit 1.0 hard set. It has no default RIR, so a myo-rep set with no RIR entered counts as hard.
Drop set: each drop has a default RIR of 0 and credits 0.5 of a hard set, and the drops after one top set add at most 1.0 set. The top set counts as normal.
Partials: credit 1.0 hard set when hard, but partial sets never set PRs.
Logged hard sets are credited to muscles with the same fractional ratings as planning.

sections.heading: Weekly targets and your level
body: Each muscle has a weekly minimum, a sweet spot and a point where extra sets stop adding much. All three are in effective sets per week.
Each target carries an evidence tag: evidence when studies measured that muscle directly, extrapolated when pooled data is stretched to it, and modeled when it is a coaching choice.

points.text: Chest at Intermediate: at least 8 weekly sets, a sweet spot of 12 to 18, and smaller returns past 20.

quotes.text: 8 weekly sets, a sweet spot of 12 to 18, and smaller returns past 20

points.text: Beginners grow on less, so the same muscle starts lower: chest at Beginner is at least 6 weekly sets, a sweet spot of 9 to 15.5, and smaller returns past 20.

quotes.text: 6 weekly sets, a sweet spot of 9 to 15.5, and smaller returns past 20

points.text: More weekly hard sets per muscle went with more growth, with diminishing returns at higher volumes. The exact numbers for each muscle are coaching choices built on that.

sections.heading: Needs sets, in range and over
body: One rule decides each muscle's weekly status, and the summary, the check and the count of muscles that need sets all read it, so they always agree.
Needing sets is the only status that fails the weekly volume check, together with being far over.

points.text: Needs sets: x < min, where x is the exact weekly total.
In range: min <= x <= diminishing.
Over: diminishing < x <= diminishing x 1.25. Far over: x > diminishing x 1.25.
Example: chest at Intermediate with 6.5 weekly sets needs sets, because the minimum is 8.

sections.heading: The weekly stimulus curve
body: The curve turns weekly sets into a share of the modeled maximum so you can see diminishing returns. It compares plans; it does not measure growth.
Its shape is a modeling choice loosely based on meta-analyses that found more sets help, with each extra set adding less.

points.text: At its weekly minimum every muscle sits at 60% of the modeled maximum, a rule of thumb.
Weekly sets count at face value: there is no discount for doing many sets in one workout. How sets land within a workout is shown by Payoff instead.

sections.heading: Payoff in one workout
body: Within one workout, each extra set for a muscle adds less growth signal and a bit more fatigue. Payoff puts both on one percentage scale for each muscle on each day.
It is a model for spotting where sets stop paying off in a single workout, not a measurement. Weekly volume is still what drives growth.

points.text: Payoff = stimulus minus fatigue. Highest in the sweet spot; below zero means extra sets cost more recovery than they build.

quotes.text: Payoff = stimulus minus fatigue. Highest in the sweet spot; below zero means extra sets cost more recovery than they build.

points.text: Stimulus rises fast and then flattens: about 63% at 4 hard sets, 78% at 6 and 92% at 10.
Fatigue grows a little faster with every set, and faster again for exercises that tire you more, like heavy squats.
For a machine chest press, Payoff peaks near 5 sets and drops to zero near 13.
For a heavy barbell lift like the back squat it peaks near 4.1 sets and reaches zero near 10; for isolation work it peaks near 5.5 sets.
On the plan body map a muscle is green while its next set still pays, amber once it is past the peak, and red when Payoff drops below zero. Muscles with under 1 hard set that day get no colour.

A large per-workout analysis found growth kept rising with more sets in one session, with diminishing returns, and could not detect extra benefit past about eleven fractional sets. It is a preprint and a conference abstract, not a peer-reviewed paper.

sections.heading: Per-workout cap and the suggestion buttons
body: Nothing changes your plan unless you tap a button, and Undo puts it back exactly.

Make it more efficient trims sets that sit past a muscle's Payoff peak, or swaps to a less tiring exercise, and never takes a muscle below its weekly minimum. Push for max growth adds sets toward the top of each muscle's sweet spot.

points.text: Push for max growth never goes past the per-workout cap: 10 effective sets for chest, 10 for biceps and 6 for forearms at Intermediate.
Going over that cap only shows an info note, because weekly sets still count at face value.

sections.heading: On plan in the weekly review
body: The review compares credited sets you logged with the sets on your board, muscle by muscle.
A small margin stops rounding from marking a muscle as behind.

points.text: A muscle is on plan when credited done >= planned - margin, with a margin of 0.5 credited sets.
Mid-week, planned = routine sets Monday through today.

quotes.text: Mid-week, planned = routine sets Monday through today.

points.text: Example: with 12 planned chest sets, 11.5 done is on plan and 11 done is not.

sections.heading: Program warnings tied to volume
body: The program checks look at single workouts and the whole week. Each flag says what is off, why it matters and what to do, and the plan shows only the most important ones.
These limits are coaching rules of thumb, not measured cut-offs.

points.text: A day with more than 20, 24 or 28 hard sets (Beginner, Intermediate, Advanced) gets a warning, and an info note when it is within 4 of that cap.
More than 5 sets of one exercise in a day gets a warning to split it or cut sets.
A day counts toward frequency when the muscle gets at least 2 effective sets that day; a muscle trained that way on fewer than 2 days gets an info note.
Two solid sessions for the same muscle too close together trigger a note to allow at least 48 hours between hard sessions.

notes: Every number in this page's points is quoted from a data file or computed from one; check_education validates each quote against the live files.

vol14 rewrite: face-value weekly volume, 60% at the minimum, one weekly status rule, Payoff per muscle per workout, per-workout cap as an info note plus the two suggestion buttons. Payoff constants are Modeled.
Worked-example inputs are marked as examples; the results are recomputed from the files.
